scope: Datasheet, connectivity, layout and nominal mechanical review for a first prototype. No physical board measurements or USB/RF certification.

power.keyboard: Mini-DIN pin 4 remains an input. TPS2116 selects it when USB-C is absent. DE9 pin 7 supplies are not connected together or used as inputs.
power.usb_priority: USB-C is VIN1; keyboard is VIN2. MODE follows VIN1. 30k/10k PR1 divider gives nominal 4.0V priority threshold, approximately 3.63-4.39V with datasheet reference and resistor tolerances. Reverse-current blocking separates sources.
power.takeover_limit: Source takeover is automatic, but arbitrary supply droop and cable impedance can still reset the board. Do not promise interruption-free operation until measured.
power.usb_power_policy: No PD negotiation or Type-C current-advertisement detection. Use an adequately rated 5V supply for normal operation; >=1A is the prototype test recommendation. Hold RECOVERY before connecting a PC to avoid starting the normal host/peripheral load on an unconfigured USB port.
power.amiga_budget: The A4000 published keyboard rating is 100mA. Prior-board operation does not establish r7's radio/MCU/OLED/two-peripheral budget. Measure board and peripheral current before enabling those loads from the keyboard source.
power.host_branch: TPS22918 disconnects host load and 220uF reservoir during recovery. CT=10nF gives approximately 26.55ms 10-90% rise at 5V and 33mA typical capacitor charging current, excluding peripherals and tolerances. The shared 500mA-hold PTC is not a precise electronic current limit.
power.host_voltage_margin: MF-NSMF050-2 specifies 0.70 ohm maximum post-trip resistance at its stated test conditions: 0.35V loss at 0.5A before switches, copper and connectors. Two ports are not each guaranteed 500mA. Verify USB-A voltage at intended load, source minimum, cable resistance and temperature; reduce allowed load if necessary.
power.direct_usb_capacitance: 4.7uF plus 100nF directly on VBUS. Other bulk capacitance is behind power switches. Soft-start is not proof of USB inrush compliance.
power.isolation: Q1 enables U2/U3 only when keyboard power is present. Q3 overrides this in recovery. Bus-switch Ioff behavior prevents signal back-powering when 3V3 is absent. Confirm connector leakage on hardware.

recovery.cold_entry: Hold the external RECOVERY button while connecting USB-C, wait >=0.1s, then release. Works without Amiga power or valid application firmware, with normal RP2350 OTP configuration.
recovery.warm_entry: With USB-C already powered, press/release RECOVERY. RUN resets the RP2350, the latch holds BOOTSEL low, and the USB switch selects the PC.
recovery.startup: USB_PRESENT is produced by a 5V-tolerant, Ioff-rated LVC Schmitt buffer. The HCS74 clear input has 100k/100nF delay. With the button held during startup both asynchronous inputs can be low; the documented Q=Qbar=1 state is safe while RUN holds reset and D2 clamps host enable. Waiting before release lets clear become inactive while preset still holds recovery.
recovery.host_clamp: R20=100k and BAT54W clamp ON to RUN while reset is held. Clamp current is below 35uA; the selected diode specifies <=0.24V at 0.1mA at 25C, versus U11 VIL(max)=0.5V. Temperature and actual startup ramps remain prototype checks.
recovery.bootsel: AO3400A pulls QSPI-CS low through 1k against 10k pull-up; nominal strap voltage about 0.3V. This is hardware ROM entry, without firmware double-tap or reset-handler dependence.
recovery.exit: USB removal clears the latch but does not itself reset the MCU. With Amiga power remaining, press/release the button to boot normally. For USB-only normal operation, unplug/reconnect without holding it.
recovery.limits: Do not program OTP settings that disable ROM USB boot. Verify erased/invalid application flash recovery on the first board. This review is not a timing simulation or measured startup result.

clock_and_usb.clocks: Keep two independent 12MHz crystals. RP2350 uses its reference-design load network; CH334P uses its internal approximately 16pF loads per pin. Verify crystal ESR, startup and frequency on hardware with a low-capacitance probe.
clock_and_usb.speed: RP2350 native USB is full speed, 12Mbit/s. The hub does not make its upstream link high speed.
clock_and_usb.routing: USB main pairs remain on outer layers. L2 has no signal tracks. Slow L3 routes were removed from a 0.6mm corridor beyond bottom USB copper; added local ground-return vias at layer transitions. See board-audit.json and plane plots. Pad/via antipads remain and require the normal layout review.
clock_and_usb.protection: TPD2EUSB30 protects each used external data channel. C4 is 220uF/10V low-ESR polymer, 176uF minimum at initial -20% tolerance. No extrapolated compliance claim from DRC.

prototype_tests_in_order: Inspect assembly orientation and resistance to ground before power. Use current-limited bench supply first; measure SYS_5V, 3V3, 1V1 and regulator startup without USB peripherals.

With Amiga disconnected and application flash erased/invalid, hold RECOVERY, attach PC USB-C, release after 0.1s. Confirm ROM drive, successful flash and repeatability across slow/fast ramps and button bounce.
Scope RUN, RECOVERY_CLR, BOOTSEL, USB_HOST_ENABLE and host VBUS during cold and warm recovery. Confirm host power is held off and startup current stays within the service-port budget.
Test keyboard-only, USB-only and both supplies; connect/remove either source and measure reverse current into the inactive connector and signal leakage with Amiga off. Record resets during takeover.
Measure idle, radio peak and display current. Establish a permitted keyboard-only peripheral budget from the actual Amiga and cable before enabling radio or two devices.
At intended USB-A loads, measure VBUS droop and hot-plug behavior, including 220uF charging, PTC voltage loss and temperature. Do not infer 500mA per port from the shared fuse.
Build r7 firmware with the new GPIO map, RM2 control and USB hub support. Implement/test SH1106 addressing if still absent. Verify two USB HID devices, both DE9 ports and mini-DIN keyboard.
Check both 12MHz oscillators, USB enumeration/recovery reliability, radio operation and antenna clearance in the assembled enclosure.
Dry-fit the retained OLED, nylon mounts, case, connectors and cables. Check USB shield-tail pockets, 1mm-PCB connector retention, recovery access and snap fits.
